name: AI Deep Dive — NVDA — 2026-02-15
rationale: NVIDIA remains the undisputed king of the AI infrastructure buildout (Rule of 40 score: 128.51), with Data Center revenue exploding >100% YoY. While 60%+ net margins are likely peak and will compress as competition (AMD, custom ASICs) arrives, the sheer backlog for Blackwell/Rubin chips supports a strong 3-year wide-moat thesis. However, valuation at $4.5T market cap demands flawless execution; any cyclic slowdown or margin compression could trigger a significant correction.

bear.rationale: Competition from hyperscaler custom silicon checks pricing power. Margins compress from 55% to 45% as supply glut emerges in 2027. AI capex cycle slows down.

base.rationale: Sustained AI infrastructure boom through 2028. Blackwell ramp succeeds. Margins normalize slightly to 50% but volume compensates. Dominance in inference training holds.

bull.rationale: Sovereign AI and physical AI (robotics) drive a second supercycle. Margins hold at record levels due to software/services mix shift (NIMs). $10T+ market cap potential.

aiThesis.rationale: NVDA is priced for perfection but executing perfectly. The raw financial strength (Rule of 40 > 120, Piotroski 8/9) confirms fundamental health. The main risk is cyclicality of capex, not competitive displacement in the near term. Base case targets $320+ by 2030, offering solid upside even from $180 levels.

name: AI Deep Dive — NVDA — 2026-02-15
rationale: NVIDIA is executing a near-perfect AI infrastructure monopoly with 62.5% revenue growth and 53% net margins—numbers that defy gravity for a $4.5T company. The Blackwell/Rubin chip roadmap secures dominance through 2028, but the valuation (24x forward P/E) leaves zero room for error. Competition from AMD and hyperscaler custom ASICs will inevitably compress margins from their current peak. The bull case hinges on sovereign AI and robotics creating a second supercycle; the bear case assumes a 2027 capex slowdown as enterprises digest existing capacity.

bear.rationale: AI capex cycle peaks in 2026, then contracts as enterprises hit saturation. AMD/ASIC competition forces 20% price cuts. Margins compress to 42% (still elite, but down from 53%). Regulatory scrutiny on chip exports to China intensifies. Multiple contracts to 18x as 'growth story' narrative fades.

base.rationale: Sustained AI infrastructure buildout through 2028 driven by enterprise AI adoption and inference workloads. Blackwell ramp successful but margins normalize to 48% as mix shifts toward lower-margin inference chips. Market share holds at 80%+ in training. Modest buybacks continue. Fair multiple of 26x reflects mature growth profile.

bull.rationale: Sovereign AI (governments building national AI infrastructure) and Physical AI (robotics/autonomous systems) trigger a second supercycle. NVIDIA's CUDA moat proves unassailable; software/services (NIMs, Omniverse) expand to 25% of revenue at 70%+ margins. Margins hold near-record levels. $10T+ market cap potential by 2030.

aiThesis.rationale: NVDA is the rare mega-cap executing flawlessly while priced for perfection. The fundamental strength is undeniable (Rule of 40 >120, Piotroski 8/9), but the valuation embeds aggressive growth assumptions. The key insight: this is NOT a 'bubble'—the earnings are real and growing—but it IS vulnerable to cyclical capex slowdowns. Base case targets $290-320 by 2030, offering 60%+ upside from current levels, which justifies a BUY rating despite the premium valuation. The main risk is timing: if you believe AI capex peaks in 2026, wait for a pullback. If you believe we're in the early innings of a decade-long buildout, buy here.
